rationale: Each horizontal pair becomes one cell: [3,3] yields 3, while [0,1] and [3,0] yield 0. Only uniform nonzero pairs survive.
Each 3x3 block becomes 5 if it contains any nonzero cell. In the third demonstration, empty top-left and middle-right blocks yield 0, while both solid and partially occupied blocks yield 5.
Horizontal pairs reduce by the most common colour, including background: [2,2] yields 2 and [0,2] yields 0 under the demonstrated tie behavior.
Each vertical pair becomes one cell by counting background too: the first demonstration preserves paired 3s and 1s, while vertical [1,0] and [2,0] yield 0.
Only solid nonzero 2x2 blocks survive. The second demonstration maps three 2s with one zero to 0, but its solid four-1 block to 1.
Each 3x3 block yields its colour only when every cell is that nonzero colour. The second demonstration preserves solid 1 and 2 blocks but maps the partially filled 3 block to 0.
Uniform nonzero 2x3 blocks retain their colour; all other blocks yield 0. In the third demonstration, five 2s and one zero yield 0, while six 2s yield 2.

Every occupied 2x3 block becomes 5 regardless of its source colour or occupancy count. The first demonstration's partially occupied lower third block yields 5, while empty lower first and fourth blocks yield 0.
Each 2x3 block selects its most common nonzero colour, ignoring zeros. The first demonstration's block containing four zeros and two 2s yields 2; empty blocks yield 0.
Vertical pairs retain a colour only when both cells equal that nonzero colour. The third demonstration preserves [2,2] and [1,1], while [2,0] yields 0.
